messages:
Maya Patel: Heads up — planning to start deprecating shared API keys next quarter. Proposal is an adapter that exchanges an existing legacy key for a short-lived JWT that carries service identity + audience. Want feedback on compatibility/backwards-compat tradeoffs and a rollout sketch. @Carl Nguyen fyi :eyes:

Carl Nguyen: High-level question — how do we plan to map existing RBAC semantics into the new JWT claims? Lots of services currently read role flags off the API key record. If we change shape, do we require every service to change?

Maya Patel: Good call. Plan is to keep role semantics but surface them as a `roles` claim on the JWT. Adapter will translate legacy flags -> normalized role IDs. Services that keep reading the API key record will continue to work during opt-in: adapter emits both `x-legacy-role` header (for pass-through) and the JWT. Over time we flip services to read JWT first. Default behaviour for unmapped/unknown roles is to emit a `roles: ["read-only"]` fallback to avoid silent elevation.

Jen Ortiz: For SDKs — we should auto-exchange inside clients so most customers are traffic-agnostic. SDK does: detect legacy key -> call adapter -> use returned token and refresh when TTL < 60s. Minimal API change.

Leo Zhang: Question about scoping: many svc-to-svc calls rely on project-scoped keys. How does adapter convey project/org context? We need org_id and project_id in claims, and `aud` should be the target service id to avoid token reuse across backends. Also, what about cross-project calls (service in prod A calling prod B)?

Maya Patel: Yes — adapter will attest org_id and project_id in claims; `aud` will be strict (service:<target>) unless caller asks for broader audience (requires admin consent). For cross-project calls, adapter verifies caller’s permission to act on target project and includes a `delegation` entry when allowed. Everything logged to audit.

security-bot: RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026/service-auth-adapter (automated link) — please link any follow-ups there.

Carl Nguyen: Rollout concerns: we must avoid thundering exchanges on go-live. Suggest canary the adapter behind the existing API gateway, enable exchange-only for 10% of traffic and rate-limit exchange endpoint per API key. Also need a fallback path when adapter unavailable.

Maya Patel: Proposed rollout: 1) adapter available opt-in for 8 weeks (customers/SDKs can exchange voluntarily). 2) Gradual canary where gateway auto-exchanges for selected tenants, monitor error/latency. 3) Mandatory exchange after 8 weeks with a 2-week grace header period where gateway emits `Warning: legacy-key-deprecated`. We'll add metrics: exchange_success, exchange_latency, exchange_rate_limited. :hammer_and_wrench:

Jen Ortiz: Exchange flow prototype (for SDKs/runtime):
```
POST /v1/adapter/exchange HTTP/1.1
Host: auth.redwood.internal
Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_...
Content-Type: application/json

{ "target": "svc:billings", "ttl": 300 }

# response
{ "token": "eyJhbGciOiJI...", "expires_in": 300 }
```
SDK refresh pattern: if token.expires_in < 60 -> re-exchange.

Leo Zhang: If adapter is down, a safe fallback is gateway pass-through of legacy key with an added `X-Legacy-Auth-Warning` header and `Retry-After` for SDKs. But we should avoid permanent pass-through — TTLs must be short (<= 5m) and adapter health is a first-class SLO.

Carl Nguyen: Also need a migration checklist: docs for services, SDK changes, telemetry dashboards (per-tenant exchange rate, failures, latency), runtime feature flag to flip reading order, incident runbook for adapter failures. Who owns the runbook?

Maya Patel: I'll draft the RFC follow-up PR with the checklist and a runbook stub. Volunteers for runbook + telemetry? @Jen Ortiz and @Leo Zhang? :thumbsup:

Jen Ortiz: Happy to own SDK rollout and client docs.

Leo Zhang: I can own service-side changes and telemetry dashboards. Will add `aud` validation tests to the integration suite.

sre-bot: Deploy bot: canary adapter stack 2026-03-23T14:02 scheduled (reminder).

Maya Patel: Awesome — thanks team. I'll open the follow-up PR and assign tasks. Will link monitoring dashboards in the PR. End-state: no shared key usage in 3 months.
